title.suggested: Wray's Column: Allen first to regain the heavyweight title

summary.suggested: The St. Louis Post-Dispatch argued Tom Allen, late keeper of the Champion's Rest, was the first heavyweight to regain the title, beating Mike McCoole in seven rounds in 1873 after a biased verdict on Chouteau Island.

metadata.notes: Page image is the continuation page: St. Louis Post-Dispatch, Sunday Morning, December 13, 1936, page 2D. Page one masthead not seen.

facts.fact: Allen ran the Champion's Rest, a sawdust-floored tavern on Market Street near Seventh, St. Louis, opened after his retirement from the ring and operated until his death
places: Champion's Rest, Market Street near Seventh, St. Louis

facts.fact: Allen fought Mike McCoole on Chouteau Island in the Mississippi; Allen was winning but the referee, intimidated by roughs, gave the verdict to McCoole, who claimed the title for four years
Allen met McCoole again and cut him to ribbons, making him quit in seven rounds and regaining his title

notes: The column contains errors: it says Allen died in 1904 (he died in 1903) and settled in St. Louis 'in the early sixties' (he came to America in 1867). These are not recorded as facts.
